title: Cohort Scheduler and Failsafe Rollback Runbook for Model Variant Experiments
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create a production-ready experiment manager that schedules cohort exposures, runs sequential statistical checks, and triggers deterministic failsafe rollback policies. This work ties together traffic choreography (cohort allocation, shadow lanes), lightweight sequential hypothesis testing for multiple metrics, and an operator-friendly rollback/playbook surface that can be invoked automatically or manually. The goal is a single, reusable orchestration primitive teams can adopt for canary, A/B, and shadow experiments with clear safety budgets and audit trails.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort scheduler API supports percentage, timeboxed, and cohort-based exposures
Sequential statistical checks implemented for primary and two secondary metrics with configurable alpha spending
Auto-rollback rule triggers on sustained metric degradation for N windows and creates an audit log entry
Dashboard shows per-cohort latency/cost/quality slices and an experiment timeline
Runbook and playbook docs published with example YAML for typical canary/A-B/shadow flows
tasks: Design cohort allocation DSL and validation rules
Implement scheduler backend hooks and traffic token generator
Integrate sequential hypothesis checker library and expose config knobs
Wire automated rollback to deployment controller and create safe revert API
Add experiment timeline and cohort metrics to Console (per-route view)
Write runbook with escalation steps, manual revert commands, and audit examples
Create end-to-end integration tests and canary smoke tests
decisions: Use alpha-spending sequential testing (O’Brien–Fleming style) for primary metric to preserve experiment power
Expose both absolute and relative thresholds for rollback triggers to accommodate low-signal metrics
Shadow traffic lanes will be considered read-only and will not count toward user-visible exposure budgets
Rollback will be implemented as a deployment controller action with idempotent guard checks and a one-click manual override

rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal-only shadow runs for two weeks on low-traffic models. Phase 2: 1% canary on non-critical routes for three days with sequential checks. Phase 3: progressive cohort increases (1% -> 5% -> 20%) with 24h stabilization windows. Auto-rollback armed at Phase 2 and later. Manual rollback playbook and escalation included.
analysis_methodology: Sequential hypothesis testing with configurable alpha spending per experiment and per-metric. Use rolling window aggregation (configurable window length) and early-stopping if cumulative evidence crosses pre-specified thresholds. Complement with Bayesian posterior checks for low-signal metrics; record intermediate snapshots for reproducibility.
risks: False positives on high-variance metrics leading to unnecessary rollbacks
Aggregation lag causing delayed detection of regressions
Misconfigured experiments can exhaust capacity if cohort bursts are not rate-limited
Insufficient observability for shadow traffic correctness
mitigation: Require at least one power analysis during experiment creation for primary metric
Default smoothing windows and minimal observation window before auto-rollback can trigger
Rate-limiter tokens and safety budget enforcement in scheduler
Add shadow validation checks that compare response distributions between shadow and baseline and surface mismatches in Console
